reporting_basis_evidence: NRB Bank Securities PLC (the sole subsidiary) was incorporated 16 March 2021, so no consolidated statements exist before FY2021; a Consolidated Balance Sheet first appears in the FY2022 Annual Report. Determined by the project's standard method (matching the recorded five-year/summary-table total assets against the annual report's own labelled Balance Sheet columns) on the two years where both a Consolidated and a Separate Balance Sheet are printed side by side: FY2022 report shows Total Assets of 74,224,372,282 (Consolidated) vs 74,676,046,707 (Separate/Solo) for 31 Dec 2022 -- the bank's own 'Five Years at a Glance' table for FY2022 reports Total Assets = 74,676m, matching the Separate/Solo column exactly (Consolidated is 452m lower). FY2023 report shows 85,305,292,244 (Consolidated) vs 85,680,280,234 (Separate/Solo) for 31 Dec 2023 -- the bank's own 'Five-Year Progression' table for FY2023 reports Total Assets = 85,680m, again matching Separate/Solo exactly. All years in this dataset (FY2013-FY2025) are therefore sourced on a Solo/Separate basis, consistent with the project's general preference for Solo over Consolidated.
notes: annual_reports/NRBBANK/ contained 12 pre-extracted annual reports (FY2013-FY2024) at the start of this work; no bank_financials/NRBBANK/ directory existed. FY2013's own report and FY2024's own 'Annual Report' (glossy) PDF are both affected by embedded-font/encoding corruption in their pdftotext extraction (see per-year notes below and each year's period_note) and were recovered via adjacent reports / freshly-sourced alternative documents instead. FY2025 was not in the archive and was freshly researched and downloaded from the bank's investor-relations page (a Dec-31 FY2025 Financial Statement had been published, signed 30 April 2026; no glossy 'Annual Report 2025' was live yet as of retrieval). All FY2013-FY2025 Q4/year-end (audited) data now has confirmed Solo-basis coverage. Q1/H1/Q3 unaudited interim data was not researched (time-boxed to prioritize completing the full annual Q4 series and its cross-report validation, per the project's stated priority order).

sources.note: nrbbank-annual-report-2013.txt (the bank's own FY2013 report, already in the archive) is corrupted by an embedded-font encoding fault: pdftotext -layout substitutes a consistent but non-standard Unicode code point for most Latin letters/digits across ~56% of its 5,032 lines (2,844 lines match the corrupted-glyph signature), including its own Balance Sheet and Financial Highlights table. The substitution is a stable 1:1 cipher and was spot-decoded manually (digits and several words verified character-by-character) to confirm Total Assets=5,966 and Total Shareholders' Equity=4,011 reproduce exactly from the cipher, cross-validating the figures taken from the FY2014 report's comparative column instead of attempting a full document re-decode. This is treated analogously to the project's 'PDF extracts to ~0 lines -> recover from an adjacent report' rule, since the specific tables needed were unusable even though the file overall is not empty. NRB Bank commenced banking operations 4 August 2013, so FY2013 covers under 5 months of trading; ROE/ROA are flagged as not comparable to later full years.

sources.note: Cross-checked as stable against the FY2020 report's comparative column (exact match to the taka). DATA-QUALITY FINDING (documented here once, applies across FY2015-FY2022): the 'General provision'/'Specific provision' rows in the five-year summary tables are cumulative BALANCE-SHEET provision-maintained stock figures, not the current year's P&L provision EXPENSE -- e.g. this report's own P&L shows a FY2019 General provision *expense* of 75.09m and Specific provision *expense* of 814.08m, which only reconcile to the five-year table's FY2019 closing balances (~348m / ~1,110m) after adding the FY2018 opening stock (273m general + 295m specific, per the FY2018 five-year table). sources.source_document: nrbbank-annual-report-2021.txt (own Balance Sheet, Solo -- last year before NRB Bank Securities PLC required consolidation)
sources.note: MATERIAL DISCREPANCY FOUND: the FY2022 report's own comparative column for 31 Dec 2021 shows Retained Earnings of 813,753,331 (Total Equity 7,507,523,939) instead of this report's own 308,711,762 (Total Equity 7,002,482,370) -- a difference of exactly 505,041,569 -- while Total Liabilities is essentially unchanged between the two presentations (54,139,901,192 in the FY2022 report's comparative vs 54,137,791,957 here, a separate and immaterial ~2.1m difference). Because Total Liabilities was not adjusted to offset the equity change, the FY2022 report's own FY2021 comparative column FAILS the balance-sheet identity (Total Liabilities + Equity = 61,647,425,131 vs its own stated Total Assets of 61,140,274,327, a 507.15m/0.83% gap), whereas this FY2021 report's own figures balance exactly (54,137,791,957 + 7,002,482,370 = 61,140,274,327). Per the project's exception for arithmetically-impossible figures, this dataset uses the contemporaneous, internally-consistent FY2021 report's own figures; the FY2022 report's comparative for FY2021 is not used anywhere.

sources.notes: RESEARCHED (2026-08-27 session): no genuine 'Quarterly Financial Statements' filings exist for 2013-2015 or 2018-2023. A full-domain Wayback Machine CDX search (cdx api, url=nrbbankbd.com, matchType=domain, all-time, ~385 distinct PDF captures reviewed) found only two isolated real filings before 2024: 'Quarterly Financial Statements Third Quarter 2016' and a March/June/September-2017 trio (all used, see below). A separate, superficially similar series of PDFs ('1st/2nd/3rd/4th Quarter Report YYYY-YYYY', July-June Bangladesh-government-fiscal-year-labelled, 2021-2024) was investigated and REJECTED: two sample downloads (4th-Quarter-Report-2021-2022.pdf, 1st-Quarter-Report-2022-2023.pdf) are RICOH-photocopier scans, only 3-4 pages long, and OCR (tesseract, Bangla text visible) confirms they are National Integrity Strategy (NIS) / Citizen's Charter compliance progress reports -- mandatory Bangladesh Bank governance filings with no balance-sheet or P&L content -- NOT financial statements, evidenced further by 'NIS-' and 'Citizen-Chartered' prefixed filenames sitting in the exact same upload folders. The genuine structural reason for the 2018-2023 gap: NRB Bank's IPO subscription ran 28 Jan-1 Feb 2024 (prospectus vetted 28 Dec 2023) and it listed on DSE/CSE around 27 Feb 2024 -- before that, as an unlisted PCB, it had no BSEC obligation to publish interim financials publicly (Bangladesh Bank's own audit-committee review of quarterly financials, referenced throughout the FY2014-2023 annual reports' governance sections, is an internal/regulatory requirement, not a public-disclosure one). This is treated as a genuine, permanent gap, not a research failure -- consistent with this project's standing rule to distinguish structural non-existence from incomplete research.

sources.note: Downloaded directly from nrbbankbd.com/wp-content/uploads/... (still live). These are the first interim filings the bank published, coinciding with its Jan/Feb-2024 IPO and DSE/CSE listing. BASIS: each filing is a single compact 'newspaper-layout' composite page containing BOTH a full Consolidated statement set (Group, upper half) AND a full Separate/Bank-only statement set (lower half, plain-labelled 'Balance Sheet'/'Profit and Loss Account' with no 'Consolidated' prefix) -- resolved via pdftoppm page-image rendering since pdftotext's column-merging garbles the two halves together. SOLO figures are used in this dataset's quarterly/2024_Q1-Q3.json, per the project's Solo-preference rule and for continuity with the Solo-basis Q4/annual series. Balance-sheet identity verified exactly for Solo in all three quarters. Cross-quarter internal consistency verified: Q2 cumulative NPAT minus Q1 cumulative NPAT equals the source's own discrete-Q2 column exactly; Q3 cumulative NPAT minus Q2 cumulative NPAT equals the source's own discrete-Q3 column exactly. EPS convention CHANGED from this vintage onward: plain 'Earnings per share (EPS)(Restated)', not annualized (contrast with the 2016/2017 vintage's 'Annualized' EPS) -- flagged explicitly in each file's period_note. Minor unresolved item: 2024_Q2's Separate Statement of Changes in Equity does not visibly reconcile opening Retained Earnings + NPAT to the closing Retained Earnings figure from the data printed on the page (a blank/unlabelled 'Cash dividend paid for 2023' row may explain the gap but no value is printed) -- the Balance Sheet's own Retained Earnings figure is used regardless and the overall balance-sheet identity still holds exactly.

Downloaded directly from nrbbankbd.com/wp-content/uploads/... (still live). BASIS BREAK: unlike the 2024 vintage, none of these three filings prints a Separate/Bank-only statement set at all -- each is a single compact page containing ONLY Consolidated statements plus explanatory notes. This dataset's quarterly/2025_Q1-Q3.json are therefore CONSOLIDATED, explicitly flagged per the project's Solo-preference rule as a basis break from the Solo-basis Q4/annual series and from 2024's Solo-basis interim quarters. Balance-sheet identity verified exactly (or to within 1 taka rounding) for all three quarters. Cross-quarter internal consistency verified exactly (Q2-cumulative minus Q1-cumulative = source's own discrete-Q2 column; Q3-cumulative minus Q2-cumulative = source's own discrete-Q3 column) across all three files. MAJOR FINDING: this is the quarter-by-quarter unfolding of the asset-quality/funding-cost event already flagged in this bank's FY2025 Q4 period_note (Net Interest Income first turning negative on a full-year basis) -- these interim filings show it began specifically in Q2 2025 (Net Interest Income swung from +506.81m in Q1 to -797.62m discrete in Q2) alongside a ~15x jump in Specific provision expense (H1: 1,162.97m vs 75.82m in H1-2024), producing a cumulative loss of -854.33m by H1 and -1,389.60m by Q3 2025 -- far more severe intra-year than the eventual full-year FY2025 result of +108.52m profit (meaning Q4 2025 alone was a very large recovery: +108.52m minus -1,389.60m = +1,498.12m swing in the final quarter alone). This Q1-Q3 quarterly detail was not visible from the annual Q4 filing alone and materially enriches the FY2025 risk narrative already in insights.json.

Downloaded directly from nrbbankbd.com/wp-content/uploads/... (still live); Q3 2026 does not yet exist as the quarter had not ended as of retrieval. BASIS: Consolidated only, continuing the 2025 pattern (no Separate/Bank-only statements printed). Q1 2026's source PDF is a RICOH MP 3555 photocopier scan (the same scanner model that produced an unusable scanned 'Audited-Financial-Statements-2024.pdf' discarded during the FY2024 annual-report research, per this bank's Q4-2024 note) -- pdftotext extracted only the cover title, so OCR (pdftoppm 250dpi + tesseract) was used; every Balance Sheet subtotal was independently verified by resumming its own component lines (all matched to within BDT 1-2, rounding), and the P&L's own '01 January to 31 March 2025' comparative column was cross-checked against this dataset's independently-sourced 2025_Q1.json and matches exactly line-for-line, giving high confidence in the OCR. Q2 2026 (H1) is a clean text export, no issues. RECOVERY CONFIRMED WITH THE BANK'S OWN EXPLANATION: the H1-2026 filing includes a BSEC-mandated 'Additional Disclosure' (its own section 3.7) explicitly attributing the FY2025 Net Interest Income decline to a non-performing-loan event that required transferring BDT 110.71 crore of interest income to interest suspense during Jan-Jun 2025, and states the NPL ratio was brought down to 7.49% by mid-2026 through management effort, resulting in a large fall in provisioning (Total provision (D): 13.41m H1-2026 cumulative vs 1,483.52m H1-2025) and a return to profit (NPAT +87.75m H1-2026 vs -854.33m H1-2025). Also newly disclosed in this vintage: a 'Start-up equity Investment' equity line item (reclassified from Other Liabilities per SMESPD Circular No. 02, per the filing's own note 3.8, with FY2025 comparatives restated accordingly and NAVPS for 31-Dec-2025 restated from 12.89 to 12.93 as a result -- noted for awareness, not used to alter this dataset's own already-finalized 2025_Q4.json, which predates and is unaffected by this later reclassification note).
